**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` function in the `cors({...})` call in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes back the request's `Origin` only if one of these is true:
- It is exactly `http://localhost:4200`.
- It ends with `.pages.dev`.
- It ends with `.workers.dev`.

Any other origin, or a request with no `Origin` header, gets `null`, so no CORS header is sent. The same block allows these methods: `GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS`. It allows these headers: `Content-Type, Authorization`. `maxAge` is `86400`.

**To add a custom domain**, edit the condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add a clause to the `if (...)` inside the `origin` function. For one exact origin, use `|| origin === 'https://play.example.com'`. Use the full scheme and host, with no trailing slash.

Don't add it to an array form of `origin`. The code comment at line 20 and `worker/src/index.md` both say wildcards don't work there. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, and that is why the code uses a function.

If you use a suffix match such as `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`, it will also match lookalike hosts. For example, `evil-example.com` doesn't match `.example.com`, but a loose suffix without the leading dot would. The existing `.pages.dev` and `.workers.dev` checks have the same weakness. They also match any origin ending that way, including `http://` ones.

After editing, redeploy the Worker. `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 covers CORS. I didn't open it, so check it for any frontend-side steps. The frontend's API base URL would also need to point at the Worker if the domain changes.
